title: Halfway protocol lattice - sketch
content:
Purpose
---
Quick personal sketch for a lightweight "halfway" protocol — a lattice-style API between client-side prefetch controller and the Redwood inference ingress/runtime. Goal: let client agents express speculative prefetch priorities and soft guarantees without needing full session handoff semantics. Keep surface area tiny and observable-friendly.

Context + motivation
- We keep seeing ad-hoc prefetch heuristics in clients (mobile/web) that are hard to reason about and opaque to runtime.
- Want a small typed surface that:
  * declares candidate prompt prefixes (or generation tasks) likely to be used soon, with confidence, urgency, and cost-sensitivity;
  * enables runtime to schedule/batch/persist candidates opportunistically and report back viability;
  * supports graceful fallback when prefetched artifacts differ from final request.
- Tradeoffs: privacy (client may not want to reveal user content), budget (prefetch costs), and consistency (stale KV/prefixes).

High-level idea (lattice view)
- Represent speculative work as nodes in a bounded lattice keyed by (session_id, slot, fingerprint).
- Each node carries: hypothesis (short text or embedding id), priority score, expected token budget, soft TTL, and an optional tag for privacy-sensitivity.
- Nodes can be refined into more specific nodes (lattice ordering); runtime merges compatible nodes and materializes cached artifacts (KV fragments, prefix logits, warmed KV cache entries).

ASCII diagram
  +----------------+      enqueue      +----------------------+
  | client agent   | -----------------> | inference ingress    |
  | prefetch ctrl  |                   | (batcher/policy)     |
  +----------------+                   +----------------------+
           |                                     |
           | status sync (partial)                | materialize/evict decisions
           v                                     v
  +----------------+                   +----------------------+
  | local store    | <---------------- | runtime cache manager|
  | (optional)     |   fetch on miss   | (KV shards, prefix)  |
  +----------------+                   +----------------------+

API shape (HTTP/JSON sketch)
- POST /v1/halfway/nodes  
  payload: {
    "session_id": "s-...",
    "slot": "compose-1", // freeform slot key used by client
    "fingerprint": "sha256:...",
    "hypothesis": "Write a short marketing blurb about feature X",
    "hypothesis_embedding_id": null,
    "priority": 0.72, // normalised 0..1
    "max_budget_tokens": 120,
    "soft_ttl_sec": 300,
    "privacy_tag": "sensitive|none",
    "client_hint": { "on_device_only": false, "allow_quantized_cache": true }
  }
- Response: {"node_id":"n-...","acceptance":"queued|rejected|deferred","estimated_cost_ms":45}
- GET /v1/halfway/nodes/{node_id}/status -> {"state":"materialized|evicted|pending","cached_artifact_refs": ["kv:1a2b","prefix:3c"]} 

Config schema prototype (yaml-ish in text)
- client config (per-app):
  prefetch:
    max_daily_tokens: 20000
    default_priority: 0.25
    budget_mode: "soft" // soft vs strict
- runtime policy (tenant/global):
  materialize_threshold: 0.6 // min priority to consider materializing
  async_batch_window_ms: 50
  tenant_quota_key: "prefetch_units"

Telemetry & observability
- Instrument every node lifecycle: submit_time, acceptance, time_to_materialize_ms, eviction_time, realized_tokens_when_used, fallback_ratio.
- Tag telemetry with: session_kind (user, background-job), privacy_tag, client_platform.
- Provide a per-route dashboard: prefetch hit-rate, cost delta (prefetch vs cold), false-positive rate (prefetch never used).

Runtime heuristics (notes)
- Materialize when: estimated_cost_ms + marginal_queue_delay < expected_user_latency_saving * value_factor. Need a cheap micro-estimator.
- Merge nodes: if fingerprints share prefix and combined estimated_budget <= shard_limit, merge into a single batchable candidate.
- Eviction: credit-based LRU weighted by priority and last-use probability.

Security / privacy considerations
- Privacy tags allow runtime to avoid persisting plaintext (only store embeddings or encrypted blobs).
- Clients must be able to mark nodes as "ephemeral" to indicate never persist beyond immediate prefetch attempt.
- Authz: leap-frog risk if session_id reused across tenants — require tenant-scoped session namespace.

Common client scenarios (examples)
1) Compose autocomplete: user taps suggestion area -> client enqueues slot "compose-1" with short hypothesis text + high priority, max_budget 80 tokens. Runtime materializes prefix logits and warms KV for common continuations.
2) Background summarization: client queues many low-priority nodes for documents user has open; runtime may opt to sample a subset to keep within quota.
3) Multi-device: device A enqueues medium-priority node; device B later queries status and may fetch cached artifact refs for faster local rendering.

Failure modes and fallback
- Prefetch gets materialized but user edits the prompt; measured fallback: if edit diverges beyond fingerprint threshold, runtime returns "mismatch" on use and client re-runs normal request.
- Prefetch accepted but later evicted: client falls back to cold path; record telemetry to tune eviction policy.

Open questions / discussion points
- Should hypothesis be opaque id (embedding-only) for privacy? Pros: smaller surface, cons: less explainability for debugging.
- Billing model: bill prefetch tokens at a discounted rate or as a separate prefetch unit? Need product input.
- Session lifecycle: when to garbage-collect nodes for long-lived idle sessions?
- Should we provide a streaming status websocket for immediate acceptance feedback vs. poll-based GET?

Next steps / TODO (personal)
- [ ] Spike: implement a tiny gateway shim that accepts nodes and returns synthetic acceptance decisions (simulate materialize/evict) -- local dev env. (ticket JIRA-7889 references this)
- [ ] Sketch telemetry dashboard layout and required histograms for product review.
- [ ] Talk to privacy/infosec re: embedding-only storage constraint; bring recommendation back.
- [ ] Draft short API spec with OpenAPI YAML once core fields settle.

Quick notes to self
- Keep the API idempotent-friendly (client retries should be deduped by fingerprint).
- Favor conservative defaults on acceptance (avoid surprise high cost).
- The lattice abstraction helps reasoning about refinement (node -> refined node), but keep initial impl flat to reduce complexity.

Signature: Marcus R. (quick pen sketch)
